label: parse-command-line-arguments-en
top_ai_sentences:
Use this when you're building developer tools, build scripts, deployment automation, or data pipelines that need
configurable inputs.
In JavaScript, commander is the most common choice, with chainable configuration.

They handle
boolean flags, positional arguments, variadic inputs, and subcommands too.
They generate help text, validate required arguments, and cast values such as --count 5 to integers.
All major frameworks support subcommands.

Click uses decorators and composes more
cleanly.

| Technology | Library | Approach | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Python | argparse | Standard library | Zero dependencies, auto-generated help |
| Python | Click | Decorator
If a script only needs a single fixed input, skip the CLI and use a function or an environment variable.
Python's argparse ships with the standard library and covers most scripts.
Argument parsing is the first thing users hit when they run your tool.
Invoke the CLI entry point as a function rather than spawning subprocesses.

picocli uses Java
annotations and works well with GraalVM native-image compilation for fast-startup CLIs.
That runs much faster than shell-based testing.

When required
arguments go missing, users should see help text, not a stack trace.

Environment variables are ideal for secrets and deployment-specific values that shouldn't
appear in shell history.

Ignoring exit codes means CI/CD
pipelines can't detect failures when the CLI always exits with 0.

CLI frameworks take the raw argument array (sys.argv, process.argv, or String[] args) and turn it into typed
values.

For hot paths where
parsing overhead matters, prefer pre-parsed or compiled options.

If a tool is
only run by other scripts, a configuration file or environment variables may be cleaner than flags.

Click exposes envvar=, and picocli exposes
defaultValue = "${ENV_VAR}".

Validate required arguments early and
show friendly errors, not raw stack traces.

Add -h and
--help flags to every CLI, because the frameworks generate them automatically.

Exit with 0 for success and a non-zero code
on failure, so calling shell scripts can spot problems.
Put shared options in a parent class or mixin to avoid duplication.
Use libraries that natively support env var fallbacks.

Eso conduce a código frágil y no mantenible.
